item.title: various: handle wolfSSL
item.description:
Some attempts at damage control, following up on https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/504446; see the commit messages in that PR for details.

I’m tempted to drop the optional support from various packages to further reduce our exposure to upstream’s odd decisions here, given the far greater number of users in the tree of alternatives like OpenSSL, Mbed TLS, and GnuTLS; cc’ing maintainers for input:

  • curl – @Scrumplex
  • haproxy – @vifino
  • riemann_c_client – nobody, but cc @algernon as upstream and contributor?
  • ustream-ssl and libubox – @fpletz, @mkg20001, @dvn0

The only packages with a default dependency on our wolfSSL package and no support for an alternative (at least in our packaging) are rpcs3 and art-standalone. cc @onny as maintainer of the latter; seems like there’s already some issues with the licensing situation there?

  • https://gstreamer.freedesktop.org/security/sa-2026-0001.html
  • https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/gstreamer/gstreamer/-/merge_requests/10903.patch

Fixes #503018.

Note: The GStreamer security advisory mentions gst-plugins-bad, but the patch applies to wavparse, which is in gst-plugins-good. I am assuming this is an oversight in upstream's post since the 1.28 release notes correctly place the fix in the gst-plugins-good section.
